{{Quote|The Zhell and the Taungs Are Names to Conjure By, But the Truth About These Long-Lost Combatants Is Hard to Pin Down|Eschul Shaywa, lead sentence of "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
"'''A LONG TIME AGO...'''" was an article [[Author/Legends|authored]] by [[Eschul Shaywa]] and published in the periodical ''[[Imperial Center Today]]'' in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]]. It focused on the paucity of available historical information on the [[Taung/Legends|Taungs]] and the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]], two groups whose [[200,000 BBY|200,000-year-old]] [[Zhell–Taung war|conflict]] was depicted in the ancient epic poem ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' despite their importance in the culture of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. Shaywa opened the article by briefly recapping the poem's composition and plot, followed by [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Mesh Burzon]]'s commentary on the connection between the ''Dha Werda Verda'' and the contemporary [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture. Military history [[Scholar/Legends|scholar]] [[Hu Jibwe]] also drew attention to the related Mandalorian war [[Music/Legends|chant]] "Rage of the Shadow Warriors."

At that point, Shaywa's article refocused on the academics' struggles to ascertain the historicity of the events of the ''Dha Werda Verda''. Both Hu and the scholar [[Arhul Manaxa]] offered comments about the disagreements on various aspects of those events, such as their exact location, date, and whether they had even happened at all. "A LONG TIME AGO..." concluded with a personal story by Shaywa in which they questioned the [[Imperial Center Guard]] trainer [[Swart Swifto]] about the deliberations of scholars regarding both the poem and the Taungs and the Zhell, to which Swifto replied that, instead of historical details, it was the metaphorical bond between all combatants that was important.

==Description==
===Introductory recap===
{{Quote|The Zhell and the Taungs have been powerful names here on Imperial Center nearly as long as civilization has existed on our planet&mdash;and that's an awfully long time. ''[&hellip;]'' But how much do you really know about these ancient warriors? Talk to scholars, and they tell you the only thing clear about the Zhell and the Taungs is just how unclear their histories are.|Eschul Shaywa, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Last_Stand_of_the_Taungs.jpg|thumb|right|300px|"A LONG TIME AGO..." focused on the historicity of the Zhell&ndash;Taung conflict (pictured) as depicted in the epic poem ''Dha Werda Verda''.]]
"A LONG TIME AGO..." was the title of an article [[Author/Legends|authored]] by the ''[[Imperial Center Today]]'' contributor [[Eschul Shaywa]]. As encapsulated in its lead sentence, the article focused on the difficulties of ascertaining the historicity of the [[200,000 BBY|200,000-year-old]] [[Zhell–Taung war|conflict]] depicted in the ancient epic poem ''[[Dha Werda Verda]]'' between the [[Taung/Legends|Taung]] [[Species/Legends|species]] and the [[Zhell/Legends|Zhell]] culture&mdash;related to that of [[Human/Legends|Humans]]&mdash;despite the prominent role both groups had in the culture of the [[Coruscanti/Legends|inhabitants]] of the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

The article began by noting that the names of the Taungs and the Zhell were an important cultural element even in contemporary [[Time/Legends|times]] on Coruscant. In contrast, concrete historical facts about the two groups continued to elude researchers despite their efforts to combine knowledge gained from both folklore and [[Archaeology/Legends|archaeological]] excavations. "A LONG TIME AGO..." then went on to briefly outline the compositional form of the ''Dha Werda Verda'' and its plot. The poem portrayed the war between the Taungs and the Zhell, including the catastrophic near-[[Destruction of Zhell|extinction]] of the latter faction and the subsequent Taung assumption of the name "Dha Werda Verda,"<ref name="Author's Cut" /> which translated as "Warriors of the Shadow"<ref name="CSWE Taung">{{CSWECite|III|225|Taung}}</ref> or alternately as "Shadow Warriors"<ref name="Author's Cut" /> or "Dark Warriors."<ref name="CSWE Taung" />

===Mandalorian sidenotes===
{{Quote|The Taungs are now extinct, but their ways have been preserved by the Mandalorians&mdash;a human culture, ironically enough.|Mesh Burzon, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
"A LONG TIME AGO..." highlighted the extent to which the ''Dha Werda Verda'' and its narrative had been ingrained into Coruscanti culture, but the article also juxtaposed it with a comment by the [[University of Byblos/Legends|University of Byblos]] [[Historian/Legends|historian]] [[Mesh Burzon]], who characterized the [[Ecumenopolis/Legends|city-world's]] veneration of the poem "odd." According to Burzon, the Coruscanti<ref name="Author's Cut" />&mdash;primarily Humans by composition<ref name="TEA">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>&mdash;held in high esteem a poem composed by a [[Alien/Legends|non-Human]] species in celebration of the near-eradication of humanity's ancestors.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

[[File:MandaloreTheUltimateWithWickedGoldFlames-KOTOR15.jpg|thumb|left|300px|The article explored the connection between the ''Dha Werda Verda'' and Mandalore the Ultimate (pictured).]]
Burzon then also noted a further fact that they considered ironical. The Taungs, after having [[Colonist/Legends|settled]]<ref name="Author's Cut" /> the planet<ref name="EGtPM">''[[The Essential Guide to Planets and Moons]]''</ref> [[Roon/Legends|Roon]], eventually moved on to the world [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]], in the process giving rise to the Taung-led [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] warrior culture. During<ref name="Author's Cut" /> his [[3996 BBY]]<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref>&ndash;[[3960 BBY]]<ref name="TEA" /> reign, the Mandalorian [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|leader]] [[Mandalore the Ultimate]] opened the Mandalorian ranks up to Humans and members of other species, and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> he<ref name="TEA" /> also ultimately became the last Taung to lead the Mandalorians, which subsequently became a predominantly Human culture.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

"A LONG TIME AGO..." contained more commentary, that of [[Salmagodro Grand Academy]] military history [[Scholar/Legends|scholar]] [[Hu Jibwe]], on the relation between the Mandalorians and the ''Dha Werda Verda'' and its contents. Hu noted the existence of the Mandalorian war [[Music/Legends|chant]] "Rage of the Shadow Warriors," which was also known popularly as "Dha Werda Verda" and the lyrics of which were provided in the article. The scholar also pointed out that "Rage" was much more recent than the poem ''Dha Werda Verda'' and expressed his belief that the chant had originated during the time of Mandalore the Ultimate.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

===Scholarly uncertainties===
{{Quote|But what of the warriors on both sides whose valor is remembered in ''Dha Werda Verda''? Of them we know almost nothing, academics say.|Eschul Shaywa, "A LONG TIME AGO..."|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Coruscant_view_EII_2.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The deep city&ndash;covered nature of the planet Coruscant was one of the aspects affecting research efforts into the historicity of the events of the ''Dha Werda Verda''.]]
At that point, Shaywa's article returned its focus on the scarcity of available historical information on the Taungs and the Zhell. [[Arhul Manaxa]], scholar emeritus at the [[University of Rudrig/Legends|University of Rudrig]], explained that the amount of time since the supposed events of the ''Dha Werda Verda'', as well as the fact that any archaeological evidence present on Coruscant would have been buried under [[Kilometer/Legends|kilometers]]-deep layers of [[City/Legends|urban]] terrain, led to a lack of consensus among academics regarding the location of the Zhell's near-destruction, the date of that event, and even whether it had, in fact, occurred at all. Furthermore, Manaxa noted that the Taungs' supposed possession of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] travel technology 200,000 [[Standard year/Legends|years]] prior resulted in speculation among scholars regarding whether it had been the Taungs or the Zhell who had initiated their conflict, whether the war had in fact taken place much later, and whether indeed it had even happened in the first place.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Hu also added that the popular conception of the Taungs and the Zhell utilizing relatively primitive [[Weapon/Legends|weaponry]] was likely anachronistic, instead arguing that the two cultures would instead have relied on such combat technology as aircraft and [[Nuclear weapon/Legends|nuclear weapons]]. Despite that, Hu expressed to Shaywa his opinion that that fact did not take away from the literary significance of the ''Dha Werda Verda'', highlighting the poem's evocative character names and imagery.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

Shaywa concluded "A LONG TIME AGO..." by relaying a personal encounter they thought would complement the views of academics expressed earlier in the article. The ''Imperial Center Today'' contributor had recently attended a "Rage of the Shadow Warriors" performance alongside the veteran [[Imperial Center Guard]] [[Swart Swifto]]. Shaywa had inquired as to Swifto's opinion on the contemporary academic thinking on the Zhell&ndash;Taung conflict and the ''Dha Werda Verda'', to which the veteran trainer simply responded that the historical details behind the narrative of the poem were irrelevant and that, in that context, it was instead the metaphorical bond shared by combatants of all times that was important.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==History==
"A LONG TIME AGO..." was published in [[2 ABY/Legends|2 ABY]] in ''Imperial Center Today'', a periodical that catered to readers on the planet that by that time was known as the Imperial Center, and was subsequently reprinted.<ref name="Author's Cut" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|This 'modern' exploration of the Zhell and Taungs was fun, and I liked how it connected the ancient era with the Mandalorians and the Empire. But it risked feeling redundant&mdash;and with ''Warfare'' way too long already, it was a logical cut.|Jason Fry|<ref name="Author's Cut" />}}
[[File:Essential_Guide_to_Warfare-cover.jpg|thumb|right|300px|"A LONG TIME AGO..." was created for ''The Essential Guide to Warfare''.]]
"A LONG TIME AGO..." was originally meant to be introduced in the [[2012]] reference book ''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]'' by [[Jason Fry]] and [[Paul R. Urquhart]]. Fry thought the section that would have served as an [[in-universe]] representation of the article was "fun" and enjoyed the connections it made between the ancient events depicted in the poem ''Dha Werda Verda'' and the later cultures of the Mandalorians and the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].<ref name="Author's Cut" />

However, ultimately the section was deemed to be potentially redundant to other material in ''The Essential Guide to Warfare'', and given the already excessive word count of the book's manuscript that Fry had submitted, it was decided that cutting the section before the book's release was "logical." It was later released in [[2013]] as part of [[Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut|''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut]], a series of articles published on the [[StarWars.com]] [[Star Wars Blog|Blog]] by Fry and<ref name="Author's Cut" /> [[Del Rey]] editor<ref name="Celestials">{{SW|url=news/star-wars-the-essential-guide-to-warfare-authors-cut-the-celestials|text=''Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare'' Author's Cut &mdash; The Celestials|int=Star Wars: The Essential Guide to Warfare Author's Cut}}</ref> [[Erich Schoeneweiss]] containing various cut content from the book.<ref name="Author's Cut" />
